title: phoradendron serotinum subsp. tomentosum
intro: Phoradendron serotinum subsp. tomentosum, commonly known as the Eastern Red-mistletoe or Woolly Mistletow, is a subspecies of mistletoe native to eastern North America. It is an evergreen parasitic plant that grows on the branches of various tree species, such as oak, maple, and hickory. The plant has been used in traditional medicine to treat various health issues, including respiratory problems, due to its health benefits in reducing inflammation and improving breathing. The bioactive constituents of Eastern Red-mistletoe include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and diterpenes, which exhibit therapeutic actions such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties.
